We need to determine appropriate criminal charge(s) for this case.

Facts: Medical equipment sales to hospital, bribery (giving kickbacks to hospital director). The defendant is a sales person (or manager) who gave bribes to a state employee (hospital director) to obtain contracts. This is a classic case of bribery (受贿) but the defendant is the bribe giver, i.e., offering bribes to a state staff. In Chinese criminal law, giving bribes to state staff is "行贿" (bribery). The hospital director is a state staff (public servant). So the charge is "行贿". Also possibly "非法经营" but main is "行贿". The description: "为谋取不正当利益，给予国家工作人员回扣人民币600万和美元20万". That's "行贿罪". Also maybe "受贿罪" is for the recipient, not the giver. So we output "行贿". The instruction: Use exact official label. In previous examples, they used "受贿". For bribery given, they used "受贿" for recipient, "行贿" for giver. So answer: [罪名]行贿<eoa>.

Check if any other charges: Could be "非法经营罪"? No. The sale of medical equipment is legal. The bribery is the main crime. So single charge.
